root.name: Semi-Slav Defense: Stonewall Defense
root.moves: 1. d4 d5 2. Nf3 Nf6 3. c4 c6 4. Nc3 e6 5. e3 Ne4 6. Bd3 f5

overview: Black sets up a Stonewall structure with pawns on c6, d5, e6 and f5 and a knight on e4, against the Semi-Slav move order. White plays Bd3 and trades the e4 knight or plays Qc2, and Black keeps a solid wall with a hole on e5. Black plays for a kingside attack or the e4 outpost, while White targets e5 and the bad c8 bishop.

white_ideas.idea: Trade the e4 knight with Nxe4 or Bxe4
Control e5 with Ne5 and Qc2

black_ideas.idea: Keep the knight on e4 and the Stonewall wall
Free the c8 bishop with ...b6 or ...Bd7

typical_structures.structure: Stonewall: pawns c6, d5, e6, f5 with a knight on e4

character.notes: The Stonewall structure is hard to break but has long-term weaknesses.

structure.notes: Locked central pawns with play on the wings.

approach.notes: A set-up Black can play against several White openings.

level.notes: Plans around e5 and the c8 bishop need understanding, not memorisation.

character.reason: The Stonewall wall is hard to break down.

soundness.reason: The Stonewall is a respected set-up.

structure.reason: The central pawns lock together and play moves to the wings.

approach.reason: Black can play the Stonewall against several White set-ups.

level.reason: It is plan-based with modest theory.

plans.reason: The Stonewall wall, the e4 knight and the c8 bishop define the play.
